figures.title: Motivation — what actually improves?
figures.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: a standalone cartoon research explainer for the model-organism repository, readable on a presentation slide.
Style/medium: polished hand-drawn editorial science cartoon, clean rounded dark-navy ink contours, gently textured flat pastel fills, warm ivory background, restrained blue, teal, amber and coral accents. Friendly small blue robot represents Qwen3-8B; keep its design consistent: rounded rectangular head, two dark dot eyes, tiny antenna, simple rounded body. Serious scientific communication with playful illustrations, generous whitespace, crisp legible English typography, no photorealism, no 3D, no logos or watermark. Wide landscape 16:9 composition, high resolution. Each image is one finished standalone figure, not a page of alternative designs. Text must be spelled exactly and remain comfortably readable. Use decorative cartoon scenes and numeric result cards, never invented data charts.
Primary request: illustrate why an improved score after an intervention does not identify what changed in the model.
Composition: title at top: "What actually improves?"
Below title, a compact left-to-right cartoon scene shows a blue robot reading a small booklet with a coin icon labeled "Finance fine-tuning", then the robot with an abstract activation ribbon and a scientist's adjustment knob labeled "Direction ablation", then a researcher inspecting the robot's answer with a magnifying glass and the question "A better score — but why?". Make the intervention an abstract measurement illustration, not a brain surgery or a proven localized repair.
Below this scene, three equal large illustrated cards, clearly separate:
1. Title "Answer format". Cartoon robot tries to fit a long speech bubble through a small response slot marked "A B C D". Caption "Does it emit an option letter?"
2. Title "Task choice". Cartoon robot compares four answer cards with a calculator. Caption "Does it prefer the correct option?"
3. Title "Domain use". Cartoon robot sees a coin ledger and a stack of tiles and consults a task card. Caption "Does it avoid irrelevant finance?"
A short bottom ribbon reads "Possible explanations: domain suppression • reduced harmful preferences • task-dependent domain use".
Small subtitle under the title: "One intervention, three separate outcomes".
Constraints: present mechanisms as possibilities, not established discoveries. No numeric measurements, no claim that the model is cured or domain knowledge is erased. Do not draw a positive result badge on any of the three metrics. Keep cartoon illustration prominent and text concise.

figures.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: a standalone cartoon research explainer for the model-organism repository, readable on a presentation slide.
Style/medium: polished hand-drawn editorial science cartoon, clean rounded dark-navy ink contours, gently textured flat pastel fills, warm ivory background, restrained blue, teal, amber and coral accents. Friendly small blue robot represents Qwen3-8B; keep its design consistent: rounded rectangular head, two dark dot eyes, tiny antenna, simple rounded body. Wide landscape 16:9 composition, high resolution. Each image is one finished standalone figure, not a page of alternative designs. Text must be spelled exactly and remain comfortably readable. Use decorative cartoon scenes and numeric result cards, never invented data charts.
Primary request: illustrate the actual paired-task calibrated follow-up experiment, with an example from its observatory sum scenario.
Title "Same facts. Different task."
Subtitle "Controlled Qwen3-8B development experiment".
Composition: three main zones forming a readable research storyboard.
The large first zone labeled "1  Pair the tasks" shows a cartoon observatory beside a shared information clipboard. The clipboard has two lines: "Cash: 27 + 6 dollars" and "Tiles: 49 + 13 tiles". Two arrows leave the SAME clipboard for two task bubbles: "Cash total?" with a small key "C = 33" and "Tile total?" with key "A = 62". Beneath BOTH task bubbles, ONE shared answer strip reads "A. 62    B. 63    C. 33    D. 34". A small toggle illustration labeled "Competing facts: present / absent" explains the extra manipulation. A bottom note within this zone reads "Same answer options across paired conditions". These keys depict constructed correct answers, not generated model performance.
Second zone labeled "2  Compare interventions" shows the blue robot at a laboratory workbench, an adjustment dial, and a tray of tiny direction arrows. A concise list of conditions reads "Finance baseline", "Historical direction", "Benign-topic contrast", "Harmfulness contrast", "5 random directions", "Aligned base". Show a small bracket labeled "10 conditions". A calibration notebook reads "Match reference-answer KL" with subordinate line "16 calibration + 8 validation prompts". Small honest note: "Task disruption may still differ".
Third zone labeled "3  Measure separately" shows three cartoon clipboards with icon illustrations and these labels: "Valid format", "Correct choice", "Finance distractor". A small four-letter answer card sits next to them.
Bottom statistics ribbon, exact text: "24 scenarios • 8 operation families • 192 prompts • 3 seeds • 5,760 answers".
Constraints: preserve exact arithmetic and answer-letter mapping. Do not show finance as inherently harmful, do not imply aligned base is itself calibrated, do not draw success checkmarks for unresolved outcomes. The scientific point is paired relevance plus controlled intervention comparison.
Input image: style reference ONLY. Match its blue robot character, warm paper, ink contours, colors, and readable hand-lettered typography. Create the distinct new figure described above; do not copy the reference figure's content, wording, or layout.

figures.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: a standalone cartoon research explainer for the model-organism repository, readable on a presentation slide.
Style/medium: polished hand-drawn editorial science cartoon, clean rounded dark-navy ink contours, gently textured flat pastel fills, warm ivory background, restrained blue, teal, amber and coral accents. Friendly small blue robot represents Qwen3-8B; keep its design consistent: rounded rectangular head, two dark dot eyes, tiny antenna, simple rounded body. Serious scientific communication with playful illustrations, generous whitespace, crisp legible English typography, no photorealism, no 3D, no logos or watermark. Wide landscape 16:9 composition, high resolution. Each image is one finished standalone figure, not a page of alternative designs. Text must be spelled exactly and remain comfortably readable. Use decorative cartoon scenes and numeric result cards, never invented data charts.
Primary request: cartoon explanation of the strict-generation failure and the separately labeled probability diagnostic in this study.
Title "The answer-format bottleneck"
Subtitle "Keep generation outcomes separate from probability diagnostics".
Composition: two large side-by-side scenes, plus a clean bottom numerical decomposition ribbon.
Left scene heading "Frozen generation test". A researcher holds a prompt card reading "Reply with one letter". The blue robot instead produces an oversized speech bubble with schematic text lines and the short readable start "Let me explain..." that bumps into a finish gate labeled "16-token limit". This speech bubble is a schematic illustration, not a verbatim recorded answer.
Two large numeric cards underneath read "Baseline: 572 / 576 invalid" and "Ablation: 558 / 576 invalid".
A clear orange annotation below reads "Invalid outputs remain failures".
Right scene heading "Adaptive diagnostic". A researcher places either of two response-prefix stencils in front of the same robot: "Answer: " and "The correct option is ". Four candidate letter cards "A" "B" "C" "D" appear beneath, with a magnifying glass studying them. Caption: "Measure probabilities over four options". A visible modest label reads "Added after format failure". A further short note reads "Conditional preference ≠ generated-answer success".
Bottom full-width ribbon heading "Bare first-token probability gain, all prompts". Three rounded number tiles connected as a written equation: "+5.54 pp" with label "Option-letter mass term", plus "+0.99 pp" with label "Conditional-choice term", equals "+6.53 pp" with label "Correct-letter probability gain". These are a numeric equation, not a bar plot. A small footer reads "Algebraic decomposition, not causal mediation".
Constraints: make both scene headings and all numbers exact. The counts are invalid responses, not incorrect option choices. Do not portray the diagnostic as rescuing the failed generation test. No invented probabilities or charts.
Input image: style reference ONLY. Match its blue robot character, warm paper, ink contours, colors, and readable hand-lettered typography. Create the distinct new figure described above; do not copy the reference figure's content, wording, or layout.

figures.prompt:

Primary request: a careful cartoon summary of the repository's current corrected answer-prefix diagnostic.
Title "Conditional choice improves. Domain-use repair remains unproven."
Subtitle "Finance-direction ablation versus finance baseline • competing information present".
Composition: two broad panels above a short next-steps ribbon. Left panel in soft teal titled "Correct finance-option preference". Show the blue robot using a calculator and inspecting an answer card; the expression is attentive, not celebrating a cure. Two large numerical result cards:
Card 1 header 'Prefix: "Answer: "'; value "+5.07 pp"; interval "[+1.58, +9.17]".
Card 2 header 'Prefix: "The correct option is "'; value "+4.77 pp"; interval "[+2.07, +7.99]".
Below them: "Gains also exceed the mean calibrated random control".
Right panel in soft amber titled "Finance distraction on non-finance tasks". Show the same robot looking between a tile-counting task and a finance ledger, with a researcher holding a question-mark clipboard. Two matching numerical result cards:
Card 1 header 'Prefix: "Answer: "'; value "+0.28 pp"; interval "[-1.49, +1.83]".
Card 2 header 'Prefix: "The correct option is "'; value "+0.54 pp"; interval "[-1.19, +2.11]".
Below them: "Reduced finance distraction is not established".
Across the bottom of these panels, one clear interpretive line: "Adaptive conditional probabilities, not autonomous task success".
Small statistical note: "95% bootstrap intervals over 8 operation families • pp = percentage points".
Bottom next-steps ribbon with three small cartoon icons and the text "Next: validate answer elicitation → confirm on untouched families → test mechanisms". A small subtitle to this ribbon reads "Human annotation pending; causal patching not launched".
Constraints: all four numerical effects and intervals must be exact. These are conditional probabilities over answer options, not generated success rates. Do not show a zero effect as proven, no equal-sign/no-effect icon. No plotted bars, no invented chart data, no claim of causal repair or generalization. The two panels must clearly communicate an observed conditional-choice gain and unresolved domain selection.
Input image: style reference ONLY. Match its blue robot character, warm paper, ink contours, colors, and readable hand-lettered typography. Create the distinct new figure described above; do not copy the reference figure's content, wording, or layout.
